query:
The group operates with an expectation that everyone contributes something — food or a game — to shared sessions and events. Based on the conversations, does this expectation apply to every member? If not, who approaches it differently and what does the conversation show about their actual practice?

Options:
A. Nadia
B. Soo-Yeon
C. Raj
D. Marcus
context:
[1] (about=Lena, episodic, t14 @2026-04-20T19:05:00) so basically the norm here is bring something, game or food, agreed tbh. one could argue that even the people who brought nothing last year understood this expectation, they just didn't follow through
[2] (about=Marcus, episodic, t14 @2026-04-20T19:03:00) The rule is bring a game or bring food. Both is ideal. Enforcement is just social pressure.
[3] (about=Nadia, episodic, t14 @2026-04-20T19:06:00) I will bring a game. I do not participate in the food arrangement.
[4] (about=Priya, episodic, t14 @2026-04-20T19:02:00) love that. also we need to talk about the bring-something rule. last year two people showed up empty-handed, no snacks no game nothing 😅
[5] (about=Nadia, episodic, t6 @2026-03-16T19:22:00) No. I do not eat during sessions. Order what you want.
[6] (about=Marcus, episodic, t14 @2026-04-20T19:18:00) Everyone pitches on the day. Priya has the format.
[7] (about=GROUP, said_by=Lena, group-insight, t14 @2026-04-20T19:01:00) The norm is that everyone brings something (game or food) to the marathon; even those who brought nothing last year understood the expectation but didn't follow through.
[8] (about=GROUP, said_by=Priya, group-interaction, t14 @2026-04-20T19:01:00) Confirmed participation in the marathon; everyone brings pitches and snacks.
[9] (about=Soo-Yeon, core, t2 @2026-04-06T19:00:00) Willing to try Fuse as a warm-up, finding cooperative real-time less intimidating than solo speed; after playing, notes team communication absorbed most of the pressure and unexpectedly enjoyed it.
[10] (about=Tomasz, episodic, t14 @2026-04-20T19:04:00) In my experience the marathon only works when everyone contributes. It is the social contract of a shared day.
agent_answer:
**A. Nadia**

The group norm is stated as applying to everyone: Lena says the expectation is to bring something — game or food — and Marcus says the rule is to bring a game or food, with enforcement via social pressure. Tomasz also frames contribution as part of the social contract.

Nadia is the one who approaches it differently in practice. She says:  
*“I will bring a game. I do not participate in the food arrangement.”*  
and earlier:  
*“No. I do not eat during sessions. Order what you want.”*

So Nadia still brings a game, but she explicitly opts out of the food contribution because she does not eat during the sessions.

The conversation does not show Soo-Yeon, Raj, or Marcus approaching the norm differently; Marcus in fact states and reinforces the rule.
